chunks: He said: Abu al-Tayyib al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Tammar narrated to us at the Great Mosque of al-Mansur during Muharram of the year 347, from Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Anbari, from Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibn al-A'rabi, from Habib ibn Bashshar, from his father, from Ali ibn Asim, from al-Sha'bi who said:
When Shaddad ibn Aws came as a delegate to Mu'awiyah ibn Abu Sufyan, he honored him, treated him well, did not reprimand him for anything in his past, and gave him promises and hopes.
Then he summoned him on a day of public assembly and said: "O Shaddad, stand before the people and speak about Ali and revile him, so that I may know your intention regarding my friendship."

Shaddad said: "Excuse me from that, for Ali has already gone to his Lord and has been rewarded for his deeds. You have been spared of what concerned you about him, and affairs have submitted to you due to your generosity, so do not seek from people what does not befit your forbearance."
Mu'awiyah said: "You shall indeed do as I command, otherwise suspicion about you is established."

So Shaddad stood and said: "Praise be to God who made His obedience obligatory upon His servants and placed His pleasure with the people of piety as preferred over the pleasure of His creation. Upon that path have their predecessors gone, and upon it shall their successors go. O people! The Hereafter is a true promise in which an Omnipotent King shall judge, and this world has a limited tenure where both the pious and the wicked eat their share. He who hears and obeys God has no argument against him, and he who hears and disobeys has no argument for him. When God intends good for His servants, He appoints their righteous to rule them, their jurists to judge among them, and places wealth with their generous. And when He intends evil for them, He appoints their fools to rule them, their ignorant to judge among them, and places wealth with their misers. And indeed, for the welfare of rulers, their companions should be righteous."

Whoever displeases you with the truth is your sincere advisor, O Mu'awiyah, and whoever pleases you with falsehood deceives you. I have advised you with what I have presented, and I would not deceive you by saying the contrary.

Mu'awiyah said: "Sit down, O Shaddad." So he sat, and Mu'awiyah said: "I have ordered wealth for you to make you self-sufficient. Am I not among the generous whom God has blessed with wealth for the welfare of His creation?!"

Shaddad said: "If the wealth you possess is yours alone, excluding what belongs to the Muslims, and you intended to collect it out of fear of its dispersal, earning it lawfully and spending it lawfully, then yes. But if it is from what the Muslims share with you and you hoarded it from them, acquiring it sinfully and spending it extravagantly, then God, exalted is His name, says:
'Verily the spendthrifts are brothers of the devils.'

Mu'awiyah said: "I think you have gone mad, O Shaddad! Give him what we set aside for him so he may leave to his family before his illness overcomes him." So Shaddad rose, saying: "The one defeated in his mind by his desires is someone other than me." And he departed without taking anything from Mu'awiyah.
ai.seo_question: What did Shaddad ibn Aws say to Mu'awiyah when asked to revile Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This narrative recounts Shaddad ibn Aws's courageous refusal to publicly revile Imam Ali (AS) at Mu'awiyah's court. When pressured, Shaddad delivers a powerful sermon on just governance, warning that God appoints the righteous or the foolish over nations according to His will, and that true advisors displease rulers with truth while deceivers please them with falsehood. Shaddad also refuses Mu'awiyah's bribe, questioning the legitimacy of distributing public Muslim wealth as personal gifts, citing Quran 17:27.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 7. He said: Abu al-Tayyib al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Tammar reported to me at the Great Mosque of Al-Mansoor during Muharram of 347 Hijra, from Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Anbari, who reported from Ahmed ibn Yahya, who reported from Ibn al-A’arabi, from Habib ibn Basshar, from his father, who reported from ‘Ali ibn Asim, from al-Sha’bi who said:
When Shaddad ibn Aws called upon Muawiyah ibn Abu Sufyan, he honoured and welcomed him, did not reprimand him for his past lapses and gave him good promises of reward.
Then one day he invited Shaddad at a public assembly and said: "O Shaddad, stand before people and speak about ‘Ali and revile his so that I know the measure of your love for me."

Shaddad said: "I beg to be excused, for ‘Ali has already gone to his Maker and has been rewarded for his deeds. And you have been sufficiently relieved of your worry about him. Now, the affairs are under your full control because of your generosity, so do not seek from people things which do not behove your magnanimity."
Muawiyah said: "You shall indeed rise to speak, otherwise (our) suspicion about you is established."

Then Shaddad stood up and said: "Praise be to Allah Who made His obedience obligatory upon His servants and placed His Pleasure with the people of Taqwa, who preferred His pleasure over the pleasure of those He created; upon that path have the predecessors gone and upon that path shall the followers go. O People, the next world is indeed a true promise, a Day on which the Omnipotent King shall judge; and this world has a limited tenure, where every pious and impious eats his share. He who listens and obeys the truth, fears no judgement against him and he who listens and disobeys, expects no judgement in his favour. Surely, when Allah intends good for His servants, He gives them the righteous people to govern them and the learned jurists to decide among them; and places wealth in the hands of the generous among them. And when intends evil for them, He causes the fools to rule over them and the ignorant to decide among them and places wealth in the hands of the misers and niggardly among them. And for the rulers, the most befitting thing is to have the righteous companies around them.

O Muawiyah, whoever displeases you for the truth, he is your good advisor and whoever seeks your pleasure by ways which are untrue, he deceives you. I have indeed, given you a good advice in whatever I have said already and I will not deceive you by saying to the contrary."

Muawiyah said: "Sit down O, Shaddad." So, he sat down. Then Muawiyah said: "I ordered for you enough wealth to make you self-sufficient. Am I not among those generous who Allah has blessed with abundance, for the sake of the welfare of His creation?"

Shaddad said: "If the wealth you possess belongs to you, to the exclusion of what belongs to the Muslims and (if) you earned and spent it in legitimate ways, after having amassed it so that it may not be squandered, then, of course, yes. And if the wealth you have, belongs to you jointly with the Muslims and you deprived them from having access to it; amassing it in abundance and then spending it excessively, then Allah, Most High, says:
’Verily, the extravagants are the brothers of the Devils’ (Al-Isra’, 17:27)."

(Upon hearing this) Muawiyah said: "I believe you have gone mad, O Shaddad! (Then turning to his people, he said), "Give him what we have set aside for him, so that he may reach his people before he gets totally demented." Shaddad rose on his feet saying: "Someone else, other than me, has lost his sanity to his desires." He then left, without taking anything from Muawiyah.
